solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Last of contingent departed in frenzy for a region of Canada

indicators.note: the pieces before it are set inside the word for frenzy

parts.note: a frenzy is a mania

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word contingent is taken

parts.note: OB is short for obiit, Latin for 'died', used on gravestones

explanation.surface: A military contingent's last member leaves in a panic, somewhere in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'departed' gives OB, the gravestone abbreviation of Latin obiit, 'he died'.
explanation.definitionFit: Manitoba is one of Canada's prairie provinces.

indicators.note: taking in, so the first piece holds the doctor's letters
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an aim is an end, a goal
MO is a medical officer, a doctor; with the 's it gives MOS

explanation.surface: A medic's blunder ends up being accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AIM into MIA, which takes in MOS. 'bloomer' reads as a mistake, but it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimosa is a flowering shrub with fluffy yellow blossom, a plant that blooms.

clue.text: Iron panel forged to unequalled standard

indicators.note: metal that is forged is hammered into a new shape, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A wrought iron sheet made to the highest quality.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonpareil is a person or thing without equal, a model of excellence.

indicators.note: around, so the article goes round the word for one

parts.note: the is the definite article
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about an aristocrat of times past.
explanation.definitionFit: A thane was a landholding nobleman in Anglo-Saxon England and medieval Scotland.

clue.text: Ought children tuck into cheese and bread?

indicators.note: go inside, so these pieces are placed within the cheese

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
ought is a variant of aught or nought, zero, giving O

explanation.surface: Should the kids eat up their cheese and bread?
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck into' reads as eating, but it signals one thing going inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Brioche is a rich, sweet French bread made with eggs and butter.

indicators.note: rejected things are turned back, so the combined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: rot is rubbish, nonsense
litter is straw bedding for animals, a bed

explanation.surface: A bankrupt person throws out junk and scattered waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns ROTBED round to read DEBTOR. 'Insolvent' is used as a noun: a person who cannot pay.
explanation.definitionFit: An insolvent is a person unable to pay what they owe, someone in debt.

indicators.note: contains, so the word for finale goes round the word for attention

parts.note: an ending is a finale
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A charming last act that keeps the audience gripped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something endearing inspires affection, charming and delightful.

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the article sits over the newspaper

parts.note: the is the definite article
FT is the Financial Times, the paper this puzzle appears in

explanation.surface: A paper runs a story about a robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: Theft is the act of stealing, a plain synonym for robbery.

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, so a soldier
something that served was good enough for the purpose

explanation.surface: A shy soldier did enough to get by.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved person is shy and holds back, which is what diffident means.

clue.text: Powerful person with a right to be in time

indicators.note: the pieces before it are placed within the word for time

parts.note: MIN is short for minute, a measure of time
and means with, together with

explanation.surface: An influential figure who is entitled to arrive punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin is a high-ranking, influential official, originally in imperial China.

indicators.note: with the head cut off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: in the board game Snakes and Ladders, the snakes are paired with ladders

explanation.surface: Snakes and their companions have had their heads cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: Snakes and Ladders is a children's board game; the snakes' partners are ladders, and without the head, L, they become the snakes themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Adders are venomous vipers, the only poisonous snakes native to Britain.

definitions.meaning: to shy is to throw, as at a coconut shy
a company of actors in a play

explanation.definitionFit: To shy a stone is to throw it; a play's company of performers is also its line-up.

parts.note: the take is the money earned, the profits

explanation.surface: A society makes money from what it has invested.
explanation.definitionFit: A stake is money put into a venture, so it is an investment or share.

indicators.note: lets in, so the first piece holds the others

parts.note: a charter is a binding written grant or agreement, a bond
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: James Bond confesses to having a chill in his constitution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007, but it is a binding agreement, CHARTER, which holds A and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's character is their basic nature or makeup, their constitution.

clue.text: The Parisian follows requirement for a sewer

indicators.note: the French article comes after the word for requirement

parts.note: a need is a requirement
LE is French for 'the', as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: The French come after what a drainage system needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' reads as a drain, but it is one who sews: a needle sews.
explanation.definitionFit: A needle is the tool that does the stitching, so it is literally something that sews.

clue.text: Hold back fairy caught by cunning insect

parts.note: to dam water is to hold it back

indicators.note: held within, so the fairy goes inside the word for cunning

parts.note: sly means cunning
an elf is a fairy

explanation.surface: Restraining a fairy that has been trapped by trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: A damselfly is a slender insect related to the dragonfly.

parts.note: a court tries, or examines, a case
TE is a note of the sol-fa scale, also spelt ti

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a message in an Italian harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Trieste is a seaport city in north-east Italy on the Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Homicide has sovereign tucking into more rum

indicators.note: going inside, so the coin's letter is placed within the comparative

parts.note: rum means odd, so more rum is stranger
a sovereign is a pound coin, and L stands for pound

explanation.surface: A murder case in which a king drinks yet more rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homicide' here is the person who kills, an old sense. 'rum' reads as the drink but means odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Homicide can mean a killer as well as a killing, and a strangler is a killer.

indicators.note: something badly made is put together wrongly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Soak food, and a poor light meal results.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream tea is a light afternoon meal of tea with scones, jam and clotted cream.

parts.note: to roll a lawn or dough is to even it, make it flat
a mop is a cleaning tool

explanation.surface: Even a cleaning lady puts on a fine display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' reads as 'even so', but it is a verb meaning to flatten.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollmop is a rolled pickled herring fillet, an appetiser regarded as a treat.

parts.note: copper coins are pence, abbreviated P
to lay a plan is to devise it

explanation.surface: Police officers stage a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' reads as police, but here it is pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is a drama written for the stage.

indicators.note: the abbreviation for new is set inside the marketplace word

parts.note: the agora was the public square and market of an ancient Greek city

explanation.surface: Fresh cloth goes on sale in an Athenian market.
explanation.definitionFit: Angora is a soft fabric or yarn made from the hair of angora rabbits or goats.

clue.text: The hunter hunted for work over a long period

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so the work word sits on top of the rest

parts.note: an act is a deed, a piece of work
an eon is an immensely long period of time

explanation.surface: Pursued for a job over many years.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Actaeon, a huntsman, saw Artemis bathing; she turned him into a stag and his own hounds hunted him down.

clue.text: In favour of taking a pound in coin

indicators.note: taking in, so the word for in favour of holds the pound sign's letter

parts.note: for means in favour of
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Supporting the acceptance of a pound in cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A florin was a British two-shilling coin, worth ten pence after decimalisation.

clue.text: Penny's allowed to tuck into a portion of dessert

indicators.note: the pieces before it go inside the following ones

parts.note: a part is a portion
P is the abbreviation for penny; the 's stands for 'is', a link
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A coin is permitted to go into a slice of pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion lands after the first two letters of the portion phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple tart is a classic baked fruit pudding served after the main course.

parts.note: pa is father; the 's makes him the owner of the hand
paw is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: The product of a father's labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Papaw, or pawpaw, is a tropical fruit, the papaya.

parts.note: can is slang for a toilet
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A toilet stands next to a big stretch of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is an artificial channel built for boats or irrigation.

clue.text: Tory's skin problem leads to collapse

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the Tory party
a rash is an outbreak on the skin

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician's skin complaint brings about their downfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash is a sudden fall or failure, as of markets or a business.

parts.note: a tip is a gratuity; the 's is 'is', joining it to the next word
food or service that is off is not up to standard

explanation.surface: Hinting that a waiter's tip is too small.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a quiet warning or hint is to suggest something to them in advance.

clue.text: Merchant needed by three blind mice?

definitions.meaning: a shopkeeper selling goods to the public
the farmer's wife cut off their tails in the nursery rhyme, so they would need someone to put tails back on

explanation.surface: A trader whose custom comes from three sightless rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as RE-TAILER: one who tails again. In the nursery rhyme the mice lose their tails to a carving knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A retailer is a merchant who sells goods directly to customers.

parts.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster, gives AL
ways are habits or practices

explanation.surface: A mobster rehearses without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: something that happens at all times happens continually.

indicators.note: things gone wrong are disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An escapee is not a hunter, sadly, but the hunted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fleeing the law, a fugitive, is said to be on the run.
